title: Snap-together electric car kit for a kids' build party
tagline: Six printed parts, a motor and a battery pack: a kit designed so 16 kids could assemble a working car in minutes and spend the rest of the time customizing it
summary: A modular 3D-printed car kit I designed in Fusion 360 for a maker-themed birthday party, then reused in my after-school makerspace. The first version I'd built had kids spending the whole session assembling; this one assembles in a few steps so the time goes to making it their own.
role: I was responsible for the whole thing: client communication with the parent, budget and timeline, CAD, printing, the wheel system and running the build session.
goal_constraints:
- Assemble into a driving car with no instructions and no adult help, for kids around 8–10.
- Cheap enough to print and kit for 16 participants on a parent's budget.
- Leave most of the session for customization, not assembly.
process_md:
- Cut the base to six printed parts plus batteries, battery pack and motor; everything press-fits or snaps.
- Designed pop-on wheel hubs so kids could cut their own wheels from cardboard and glue them to the hubs.
- Modeled LEGO-compatible studs into the chassis so decorations attach without glue or mess.
- Printed a kit per child, wrote a parts list and ran the build session (photo 2).
